name: Jehezkel
overview: Jehezkel was a male Levite priest, specifically noted as the twentieth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the two sons of Aaron from whom the priestly divisions descended. His role as a priest in this division highlights his service in the organized worship system established for Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehezkel means 'G-d [El] gives strength,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with the divine empowerment of those who serve in the priesthood. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:16 and was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotations.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Jehezkel as a descendant of Ithamar, situating him within the priestly lineage that descended from Aaron's son Ithamar. Beyond this tribal and familial connection, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jehezkel's significance lies in his role as a priest chosen to serve in one of the twenty-four priestly courses established by King David, which organized the Levitical priesthood for temple service. Being from the line of Ithamar, Jehezkel represented a continuation of the priestly duties entrusted to Aaron's descendants. His inclusion in this division underscores the orderly worship system ordained by God and maintained through his appointed priests.
